cases.sentence: Свияжский взял под ___ Левина и пошел с ним к своим.
cases.translation: Svyazhsky took Levin by the arm and went with him to his group.
cases.explain: The preposition под in the idiom взять под руку (to take by the arm) governs the accusative case, giving руку.

cases.sentence: «Кажется, я имел удовольствие встретить у ___ Щербатской», — сказал он, подавая руку Левину.
cases.translation: "I believe I had the pleasure of meeting you at Princess Shcherbatskaya's," he said, offering his hand to Levin.
cases.explain: The preposition у (at the home of) governs the genitive case, giving княгини.

cases.sentence: Он держал ___ вправой, но переложил его в левую руку.
cases.translation: He held the ball in his right hand, but shifted it into his left hand.
cases.explain: Шар is the direct object of the transitive verb держал (held), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Мировой судья от меня в сорока ___.
cases.translation: The justice of the peace is forty versts from me.
cases.explain: The expression в сорока верстах (forty versts away) uses the prepositional case after в indicating distance, giving верстах.

cases.sentence: Я должен о деле в два рубля посылать ___, который стоит пятнадцать.
cases.translation: For a two-rouble matter I have to send an attorney who costs fifteen.
cases.explain: Поверенного is the direct object of the transitive verb посылать (to send), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.translation: The peasant stole flour from the miller.
cases.explain: The preposition у (from) governs the genitive case, giving мельника.

cases.translation: The peasant lodged a complaint of slander with the judge.
cases.explain: The indirect object of подал (submitted to someone) takes the dative case, giving судье.

cases.sentence: Он звал обедать, я не поеду к ___.
cases.translation: He invited me to dinner, but I will not go to him.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case of the pronoun, giving нему.

cases.sentence: Уездные предводители заходили с тарелочками, в которых были ___, от своих столов к губернскому.
cases.translation: The district marshals came with little plates in which there were balls, from their own tables to the provincial one.
cases.explain: Шары is the grammatical subject of были (were), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Секретарь громогласно объявил, что баллотируются в губернские предводители ротмистр гвардии Михаил Степанович ___.
cases.translation: The secretary loudly announced that Guards captain Mikhail Stepanovich Snitkov was being balloted for provincial marshal.
cases.explain: Снитков is the grammatical subject in apposition naming the candidate, so it stands in the nominative case.

reading.ru: Свияжский взял под руку Левина и пошел с ним к своим.
reading.question: What did Svyazhsky do at the start of the chapter?
options: Took Levin's arm and walked with him toward his own group
Left Levin alone in the hall
Argued with Levin about the election
reading.correct: Took Levin's arm and walked with him toward his own group
reading.explain: The chapter opens with Svyazhsky taking Levin's arm and going with him to his own party.

reading.ru: Теперь уж нельзя было миновать Вронского.
reading.question: What became unavoidable for Levin at this point?
reading.explain: The text says it was now impossible to avoid Vronsky.

reading.ru: «Очень рад. Кажется, я имел удовольствие встретить у княгини Щербатской», — сказал он, подавая руку Левину.
reading.question: How did Vronsky greet Levin?
options: Politely, recalling meeting him at Princess Shcherbatskaya's, and offering his hand
By challenging him to a duel
reading.correct: Politely, recalling meeting him at Princess Shcherbatskaya's, and offering his hand
reading.explain: The text has Vronsky say he was glad, recall meeting Levin at Princess Shcherbatskaya's, and offer his hand.

reading.ru: Но Левин, говоря с братом, беспрестанно оглядывался на Вронского, придумывая, о чем бы заговорить с ним, чтобы загладить свою грубость.
reading.question: Why did Levin keep glancing at Vronsky while talking to his brother?
options: He was trying to think of something to say to smooth over his earlier rudeness
He suspected Vronsky of cheating in the vote
He was waiting for Vronsky to leave
reading.correct: He was trying to think of something to say to smooth over his earlier rudeness
reading.explain: The text explains Levin kept glancing at Vronsky, trying to think what to say to make up for his rudeness.

reading.ru: «В том-то и дело, что ни то, ни сё», — сказал Вронский.
reading.question: How did Vronsky describe Snetkov's uncertain position when asked if he had agreed to run?
options: "That's just the point, it's neither one thing nor the other"
reading.correct: "That's just the point, it's neither one thing nor the other"
reading.explain: The text quotes Vronsky saying that's just the trouble, it's neither one thing nor the other.

reading.ru: Невидовский, — сказал Левин, чувствуя, что он запутался.
reading.question: What awkward mistake did Levin make when asked who would run if Snetkov declined?
options: He named Nevedovsky, realizing he had gotten confused since Nevedovsky and Svyazhsky were rival candidates
He named himself as a candidate
He refused to answer at all
reading.correct: He named Nevedovsky, realizing he had gotten confused since Nevedovsky and Svyazhsky were rival candidates
reading.explain: The text shows Levin blurting out Nevedovsky's name while feeling he had gotten tangled up, since Nevedovsky and Svyazhsky were the two candidates.

reading.ru: «Да, это забирает за живое», — сказал Вронский. «И раз взявшись за дело, хочется его сделать».
reading.question: How did Vronsky describe his feelings about the election contest?
options: It had gotten under his skin, and once involved he wanted to see it through
He wished he had never come
He was only there for Anna's sake
reading.correct: It had gotten under his skin, and once involved he wanted to see it through
reading.explain: The text quotes Vronsky saying yes, it gets you excited, and once you've taken up a matter, you want to carry it through.

reading.ru: «От того, что я считаю, что Мировой суд есть дурацкое учреждение», — отвечал мрачно Левин
reading.question: Why did Levin say he was not a justice of the peace?
options: Because he considered the justice-of-the-peace court a foolish institution
Because he had never been asked to serve
Because he lived too far from the town
reading.correct: Because he considered the justice-of-the-peace court a foolish institution
reading.explain: The text has Levin gloomily answer that it is because he considers the Mirovoi Sud (justice of the peace court) a foolish institution.

reading.ru: И он рассказал, как мужик украл у мельника муку, и когда мельник сказал ему это, то мужик подал иск судье в клевете.
reading.question: What story did Levin tell to illustrate his complaint about the justice system?
options: A peasant stole flour from a miller, and when accused, sued the miller for slander
A landowner cheated a peasant out of his land
A judge took a bribe from a nobleman
A merchant refused to pay his debts
reading.correct: A peasant stole flour from a miller, and when accused, sued the miller for slander
reading.explain: The text describes Levin telling how a peasant stole flour from a miller, and when the miller confronted him, the peasant sued the miller for slander.

reading.ru: «Я не понимаю, как можно быть до такой степени лишенным всякого политического такта».
reading.question: What did Sergei Ivanovich criticize Levin for after his conversation with Vronsky?
options: Being utterly lacking in political tact
reading.correct: Being utterly lacking in political tact
reading.explain: The text quotes Sergei Ivanovich saying he did not understand how one could be so utterly devoid of political tact.

reading.ru: «А граф Вронский? Я друга себе из него не сделаю. Он звал обедать, я не поеду к нему. Но он наш, зачем же делать из него врага?
reading.question: What was Sergei Ivanovich's stance toward Vronsky, despite personal distance?
options: He would not befriend him personally but saw no reason to make an enemy of him, since he was on their side
He considered Vronsky a dangerous enemy
He wanted to become close friends with Vronsky
He refused to acknowledge Vronsky at all
reading.correct: He would not befriend him personally but saw no reason to make an enemy of him, since he was on their side
reading.explain: The text has Sergei Ivanovich say he won't make a friend of Vronsky and won't go to dine with him, but since Vronsky is on their side, there's no reason to make an enemy of him.

reading.ru: секретарь громогласно объявил, что баллотируются в губернские предводители ротмистр гвардии Михаил Степанович Снитков.
reading.question: What did the secretary loudly announce?
options: That Guards captain Mikhail Stepanovich Snitkov was being balloted for provincial marshal
reading.correct: That Guards captain Mikhail Stepanovich Snitkov was being balloted for provincial marshal
reading.explain: The text quotes the secretary's loud announcement naming Snitkov as the candidate for provincial marshal.

reading.ru: «Направо клади», — шепнул Степан Аркадьевич Левину, когда он вместе с братом вслед за предводителем подошел к столу.
reading.question: What instruction did Stepan Arkadyevich whisper to Levin at the ballot table?
options: To place his ball on the right
To place his ball on the left
reading.correct: To place his ball on the right
reading.explain: The text quotes Stepan Arkadyevich whispering to Levin to put it on the right.

reading.ru: Подойдя к ящику, он держал шар вправой, но, подумав, что ошибся, перед самым ящиком переложил шар в левую руку и, очевидно, потом положил налево.
reading.question: What confusion occurred when Levin actually cast his ball?
options: He switched the ball from his right hand to his left at the last moment, apparently voting the opposite way intended
He dropped the ball on the floor
He refused to vote at all
reading.correct: He switched the ball from his right hand to his left at the last moment, apparently voting the opposite way intended
reading.explain: The text describes Levin holding the ball in his right hand but, thinking he had made a mistake, switching it to his left hand right before the box and apparently placing it on the left.

reading.question: What was the result of the vote for marshal?
options: The marshal (Snitkov) was elected by a considerable majority
The vote ended in a tie
reading.correct: The marshal (Snitkov) was elected by a considerable majority
reading.explain: The text states the marshal was elected by a significant majority.

reading.ru: Съев котлетку с фасолью и поговорив с лакеем о прежних господах, Левин, не желая входить в залу, где ему было так неприятно, пошел пройтись на хоры.
reading.question: What did Levin do after eating and chatting with the footman?
options: He went for a walk up to the gallery, avoiding the unpleasant hall
He returned to argue with Vronsky
He fell asleep in the small hall
reading.correct: He went for a walk up to the gallery, avoiding the unpleasant hall
reading.explain: The text says after eating a cutlet with beans and talking with the footman, Levin, not wanting to enter the unpleasant hall, went to walk on the gallery.

reading.ru: «Баллотируется в кандидата губернского предводителя дворянства штаб-ротмистр Евгений Иванович Опухтин».
reading.question: What was announced as the candidates were balloted one by one?
options: Names of candidates for the office of provincial marshal, such as staff-captain Yevgeny Ivanovich Opukhtin
The results of the previous day's vote
reading.correct: Names of candidates for the office of provincial marshal, such as staff-captain Yevgeny Ivanovich Opukhtin
reading.explain: The text quotes the announcement of staff-captain Yevgeny Ivanovich Opukhtin being balloted as a candidate for provincial marshal.

reading.ru: Неведовскому переложили, как и было рассчитано, и он был губернским предводителем.
reading.question: Who ultimately won the election for provincial marshal?
reading.explain: The text states that the votes were shifted to Nevedovsky as planned, and he became the provincial marshal.
